the decoder in the notebook 

    

  






  

    
Nobody gave it labels
The colors were added for this picture. The network only learned to rebuild images, and still the zeros, the ones and the sixes each get their own region, because images that look alike need similar codes.

    
Between the regions
Drag from one colored region to another and watch the output on the way: one digit turns into the other through shapes that are neither. Where two colors overlap (4, 7 and 9), two numbers are not enough to tell the digits apart.

    
Off the map
Move to a corner where there are no points. The decoder still draws something, confidently, although no training digit ever had a code there. An autoencoder was trained to compress, and nothing taught its decoder what to do with a code it never saw.
